Pattern: Ines's glass location.
Assumption: I defaulted to nightstand_b1 for late evening/night queries, assuming she was in bed.
Reality: On day 8, the glass was at kitchen_table_k1 at 21:30, 22:01, and sink_k1 at 22:59. It was not in the bedroom.
Correction: The glass remains in the kitchen area (kitchen_table_k1, sink_k1, counter_k1) well into the late night. Do not assume it moves to the bedroom until much later or if explicitly indicated. Check kitchen spots first for any time after 20:00.

Pattern: Ines's book location.
Assumption: I defaulted to bed_b1 for late evening queries, assuming she was reading in bed.
Reality: On day 8 at 22:19, the book was at couch_l1. Previous data also showed it in the living room (armchair_l1, couch_l1) during the day and early evening.
Correction: The book is highly variable but strongly associated with living room seating (couch_l1, armchair_l1) throughout the day and evening. Do not default to bedroom spots. Check living room seating first for all times of day.

Pattern: Ines's mug location.
Assumption: I defaulted to cupboard_k1 based on morning routines.
Reality: On day 8 at 08:34, the mug was at kitchen_table_k1. Previous data confirms it is highly variable.
Correction: Do not rely on time-of-day heuristics. Check kitchen_table_k1, counter_k1, and coffee_table_l1 as primary candidates. If unsure, ABSTAIN rather than guessing a specific room based on the time.

Pattern: Generalization error regarding Ines's items.
Assumption: I treated all of Ines's items as having the same location logic or following a predictable daily path.
Reality: Items move independently based on immediate activity. The glass was in the kitchen while the book was in the living room on the same day.
Correction: Track each item individually. Do not assume that because one item is in the kitchen, other items are in the same room. Always consider the specific item's likely current use and recent history.
